title: How often does each prime occur in seventy two, twelve and six?
description: The primes of seventy two are counted, and so are the primes of twelve and six put together. The two counts are compared prime by prime. Keeko doubts this and says twelve and six together have only two twos.
teaching_notes: One idea: when two factorisations are joined, the counts of each prime add up to the count in the whole number. Watch for students who count the twos of only one of the two numbers.

source: Observe how many times each prime factor occurs in the facto
video_script.why: The child sees that each prime occurs as many times in seventy two as in twelve and six put together.
video_script.substitution: the book's own numbers, seventy two, twelve and six
video_script.anchor: the rows of primes of seventy two, of twelve and of six, with the twos and the threes in two colours
video_script.wrong_answer: twelve and six together have only two twos
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko counts the twos of twelve and leaves out the two of six.
video_script.payoff_line: Each prime occurs the same number of times in seventy two as in twelve and six together

final_answer.value: 2 occurs 3 times and 3 occurs 2 times in 72, and also in 12 and 6 put together; the counts are the same
final_answer.spoken: each prime occurs the same number of times

maths_rules: 12 and 6 together: 2 occurs 2 + 1 = 3 times and 3 occurs 1 + 1 = 2 times
the counts match: 3 and 3 for the prime 2, 2 and 2 for the prime 3
video_script.design: The rows of primes of seventy two, twelve and six are shown with the twos in one colour and the threes in another. The counts are written under each row.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the rows 72 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3, 12 = 2 × 2 × 3 and 6 = 2 × 3 stand on the board

marks.book: the title card From your book appears
marks.rows: the three rows of primes appear, with 12 and 6 side by side below 72
marks.ask: a question mark appears between the row of 72 and the rows of 12 and 6

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the primes of seventy two.
<bookmark mark='rows'/>Seventy two is two times two times two times three times three. Twelve is two times two times three, and six is two times three.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Count how often each prime occurs in seventy two, and in twelve and six put together.

beats.on_screen: the rows stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the row of 72 with each prime counted by a small tick above it, the 2s ringed in teal and the 3s in amber

marks.tick: a tick appears above each prime in the row, one tick for each time it is written
marks.rings: the 2s are ringed in teal and the 3s in amber

narration: <bookmark mark='tick'/>In a row of primes, a prime is counted once for each time it is written.
<bookmark mark='rings'/>We ring the twos in one colour and the threes in another colour, so none is missed.

marks.given: the three rows are written under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the rows of primes of seventy two, of twelve and of six.

beats.on_screen: To find: how many times each prime occurs in 72, and in 12 and 6 put together
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how often each prime occurs in seventy two, and in twelve and six together.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: in 72 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3, the prime 2 occurs 3 times and the prime 3 occurs 2 times

marks.twos: the three 2s of 72 light up in teal with the count 3
marks.threes: the two 3s of 72 light up in amber with the count 2

narration: <bookmark mark='twos'/>Step one, count the primes in seventy two. The prime two occurs three times.
<bookmark mark='threes'/>The prime three occurs two times.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 12 = 2 × 2 × 3 has two 2s and one 3; 6 = 2 × 3 has one 2 and one 3; together the prime 2 occurs 2 + 1 = 3 times and the prime 3 occurs 1 + 1 = 2 times

marks.each: the 2s and 3s of 12 and of 6 light up with their counts

narration: <bookmark mark='each'/>Step two, count the primes in twelve and in six. Twelve has two twos and one three, and six has one two and one three.
<bookmark mark='twos'/>Together, the prime two occurs two plus one, which is three times.
<bookmark mark='threes'/>The prime three occurs one plus one, which is two times.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: compare the counts prime by prime: for 2, 3 and 3; for 3, 2 and 2

marks.pair: lines join the count of each prime in 72 to the count in 12 and 6 together

narration: <bookmark mark='pair'/>Step three, compare the counts prime by prime. For the prime two we have three and three. For the prime three we have two and two.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 2 occurs 3 times and 3 occurs 2 times in 72, and also in 12 and 6 put together; the counts are the same

marks.ans: the answer is boxed in green

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Each prime occurs the same number of times in seventy two as in twelve and six together. Joining the rows only adds the counts.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the board
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble says twelve and six together have only two 2s; the two 2s of 12 are counted and the 2 of 6 is left out; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.two: the two 2s of 12 are counted and the 2 of 6 is left out
marks.left: the 2 of 6 glows as the missing one

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks twelve and six together have only two twos.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Twelve alone has two twos, but six brings one more two.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Keeko stopped counting too early and left out the two from six.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>We must count the twos from both numbers.
